Theorem
[maximal symmetry implies constant curvature]

Source: petersen:page-0331 ↗ thm:pet-ch8-isometry-lie-algebra-dimension ↗ prop:pet-ch8-killing-uniqueness If $\dim (\iso (M,g))=\binom {n+1}2$, then $(M,g)$ has constant curvature.
Proof

↗ thm:pet-ch8-maximal-symmetry-constant-curvature \sketch Equality in the dimension bound makes the first-jet injection from section 1 an isomorphism

\[ \iso (M,g)\simeq T_pM\oplus \mathfrak {so}(T_pM). \]

Fields with zero value at $p$ realize every infinitesimal rotation, so the isotropy acts transitively on $2$-planes and all sectional curvatures at $p$ agree. Fields whose prescribed jet is $(v,0)$ move $p$ through a neighborhood, making that curvature value locally constant. Connectedness then makes it constant on $M$.

□
